points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (a tree in which each node has at most two children). Accept equivalent wording such as 'it is a binary tree with a special property'. Do not award this point for describing only the ordering property without identifying it as a binary tree.

States the left-side ordering property: for any/every node, the left child is smaller (less) than its parent. Accept equivalent wording such as 'left child < parent' or 'left subtree contains smaller values' only if the child/parent comparison is clear. Do not award if the order is reversed (left child greater than parent).

States the right-side ordering property: for any/every node, the right child is greater (larger) than its parent, equivalently the parent is smaller than the right child. Accept equivalent wording such as 'parent < right child' or 'right subtree contains larger values' only if the child/parent comparison is clear. Do not award if the order is reversed (right child smaller than parent).

rubric.notes: Full marks require identifying the structure as a binary tree and giving both ordering conditions: left child smaller than parent and right child greater than parent, for every node. Award 1 mark for the binary-tree identification, 2 marks for the left-smaller condition, and 2 marks for the right-greater condition. No marks for a generic binary tree description without the ordering property, or for reversing the order (left greater/right smaller).
